project.name: com.cwilkes.lean.touch-plus
project.description: Lightweight touch extensions for all projects.

nodes.name: LeanTouchPlus.asmdef
nodes.summary: Unity assembly definition that compiles every script in this package into the LeanTouchPlus assembly, referencing the external LeanCommon, LeanTouch, LeanCommonPlus and CW.Common assemblies.
nodes.languageNotes: Unity .asmdef files are JSON; the references array is what makes base types like LeanFingerData and CwEditor resolvable at compile time.

nodes.name: Documentation.html
nodes.summary: Official Lean Touch+ manual (v3.1.1): explains that the package extends Lean Touch and catalogs every bundled demo scene together with the component and settings each scene demonstrates.
nodes.languageNotes: Single self-contained HTML file; roughly half its 187 KB is base64-embedded WOFF fonts inside a <style> block rather than prose.

nodes.name: IDropHandler.cs
nodes.summary: Declares the single-method IDropHandler interface that marks a component as a valid drop target for LeanSelectableDrop.

nodes.name: IDropHandler
nodes.summary: Interface with a single HandleDrop(GameObject, LeanFinger) method; any component implementing it can receive objects dropped by LeanSelectableDrop.

nodes.name: LeanDragColorMesh.cs
nodes.summary: Component that paints the vertex colors of the attached MeshFilter's mesh wherever fingers drag across it, plus its inspector editor.

nodes.name: LeanDragColorMesh
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour that clones the MeshFilter mesh at Awake and, each Update, raycasts filtered fingers against the mesh to write PaintColor into the touched triangle's vertex colors.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a LeanFingerFilter (Use) field so designers choose which fingers drive the component; AddFinger/RemoveFinger let other components feed fingers in manually.

nodes.name: Paint
nodes.summary: Raycasts a finger's screen position into the mesh collider and rewrites the vertex colors of the hit triangle, rebuilding the modified color array on the cloned mesh.

nodes.name: LeanDragColorMesh_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector for LeanDragColorMesh, drawing its finger filter and paint settings inside a UNITY_EDITOR-only block.

nodes.name: LeanDragDeformMesh.cs
nodes.summary: Component that deforms a mesh by dragging its vertices with fingers, optionally pushing the result back into the MeshCollider, plus its inspector editor.

nodes.name: LeanDragDeformMesh
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour that clones the MeshFilter mesh and, per frame, moves every vertex within ScaledRadius of a dragging finger, optionally reassigning the deformed mesh to the MeshCollider.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Per-frame deformation loop: projects each filtered finger's screen delta into mesh space and displaces nearby vertices, then uploads the changed vertex array and optionally refreshes the MeshCollider.

nodes.name: LeanDragDeformMesh_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector for LeanDragDeformMesh exposing radius, camera and collider options.

nodes.name: LeanDragLine.cs
nodes.summary: Specialisation of the external LeanDragTrail that renders each finger's drag as a straight line and fires from/to/delta events when the finger is released.
nodes.languageNotes: Requires LeanTouch.RecordFingers to be enabled, because it reads recorded finger snapshots to build the line.

nodes.name: LeanDragLine
nodes.summary: Overrides LeanDragTrail's line building to draw a single straight segment between the finger's start and current position, clamped by LengthMin/LengthMax and optionally inverted or anchored at the origin.

nodes.name: UpdateLine
nodes.summary: Computes the clamped, optionally inverted straight line for a finger and writes its two positions and scaled widths into the LineRenderer.

nodes.name: HandleFingerUp
nodes.summary: On finger release, recomputes the final line endpoints and invokes the OnReleasedFrom, OnReleasedTo, OnReleasedDelta and OnReleasedFromTo UnityEvents.

nodes.name: LeanDragLine_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector extending LeanDragTrail_Editor with the line-specific width, length, invert and release-event fields.

nodes.name: LeanDragSelect.cs
nodes.summary: Component that lets a single finger drag across the screen to select every selectable it passes through, plus its inspector editor.

nodes.name: LeanDragSelect
nodes.summary: Hooks LeanSelectByFinger's finger events and repeatedly re-runs selection as the finger moves, using a nested FingerData : LeanFingerData list to remember the last selection point and honour MaximumSeparation.
nodes.languageNotes: Nested private FingerData : LeanFingerData class is the package's recurring idiom for per-finger state.

nodes.name: HandleFingerDown
nodes.summary: Starts a drag-select for a finger, optionally deselecting everything first and rejecting the drag when RequireNoSelectables or RequireInitialSelection are not satisfied.

nodes.name: HandleAnySelectedFinger
nodes.summary: Callback fired whenever the select component selects something with a finger; records the selection screen position so subsequent movement can be measured against MaximumSeparation.

nodes.name: LeanDragSelect_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector for LeanDragSelect that warns when no select component is assigned and draws the selection requirement toggles.

nodes.name: LeanDragTranslateAlong.cs
nodes.summary: Base component that drags a Transform along a target surface or path by snapping the finger's screen position onto it, plus its inspector editor.

nodes.name: LeanDragTranslateAlong
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour that converts filtered finger drags into a screen-space target point, snaps that point onto the specified surface and moves the Transform there with optional damping. Serves as the base class for the Rigidbody variant.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Per-frame driver: accumulates the filtered fingers' screen delta into the target screen point and applies the damped remaining movement to the Transform.

nodes.name: TryGetSnappedWorldPosition
nodes.summary: Projects a candidate world position onto the configured target surface, returning false when no valid snap point exists.

nodes.name: UpdateTarget
nodes.summary: Resolves the current screen target into a snapped world position and stores the remaining delta consumed by the damping in Update.

nodes.name: LeanDragTranslateAlong_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector for LeanDragTranslateAlong and the base editor its Rigidbody variant extends.

nodes.name: LeanDragTranslateAlongRigidbody.cs
nodes.summary: Rigidbody flavour of LeanDragTranslateAlong that applies the snapped movement in FixedUpdate via physics instead of writing the Transform directly.

nodes.name: LeanDragTranslateAlongRigidbody
nodes.summary: Subclass of LeanDragTranslateAlong that overrides SnapPosition, moves the body inside FixedUpdate so physics stays consistent, and leaves Update to input accumulation only.

nodes.name: FixedUpdate
nodes.summary: Physics-step movement: converts the pending snapped target into a Rigidbody position or velocity change so collisions are respected.

nodes.name: LeanDragTranslateAlongRigidbody_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for the Rigidbody variant, extending LeanDragTranslateAlong_Editor so the shared fields are drawn once.

nodes.name: LeanDragTranslateRigidbody.cs
nodes.summary: Component that drags a 3D Rigidbody with the fingers, moving it in FixedUpdate toward the finger's screen point with optional damping.

nodes.name: LeanDragTranslateRigidbody
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour requiring a Rigidbody; tracks a target screen point from the filtered fingers in Update and drives the body toward the corresponding world point in FixedUpdate.

nodes.name: FixedUpdate
nodes.summary: Applies the pending drag to the Rigidbody on the physics step, converting the screen target into a world velocity or position change.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Accumulates the filtered fingers' screen movement into the target screen point, resetting the target when no fingers remain.

nodes.name: LeanDragTranslateRigidbody_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector for LeanDragTranslateRigidbody drawing the finger filter, camera and damping fields.

nodes.name: LeanDragTranslateRigidbody2D.cs
nodes.summary: 2D counterpart of LeanDragTranslateRigidbody: drags a Rigidbody2D with the fingers through the physics step.

nodes.name: LeanDragTranslateRigidbody2D
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour requiring a Rigidbody2D that mirrors the 3D drag component's Update/FixedUpdate split using 2D physics APIs.
nodes.languageNotes: Near-duplicate of the 3D version; Unity's separate 2D physics API is why the two exist side by side rather than sharing a base class.

nodes.name: FixedUpdate
nodes.summary: Moves the Rigidbody2D toward the tracked screen target on the physics step.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Accumulates filtered finger movement into the target screen point each frame and clears it when the drag ends.

nodes.name: LeanDragTranslateRigidbody2D_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector for the 2D Rigidbody drag component.

nodes.name: LeanDrop.cs
nodes.summary: Drop target component: implements IDropHandler and raises an OnDropped UnityEvent with the dropped GameObject.

nodes.name: LeanDrop
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour implementing IDropHandler.HandleDrop, forwarding each dropped GameObject to the inspector-wired OnDropped event.

nodes.name: LeanDrop_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector for LeanDrop drawing the OnDropped event.

nodes.name: LeanDropCount.cs
nodes.summary: Drop target that counts how many objects have been dropped on it and raises match/unmatch events when the count enters or leaves a configured range.

nodes.name: LeanDropCount
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour implementing IDropHandler that increments Count on each drop and invokes OnCount, OnMatch and OnUnmatch depending on whether Count sits inside MatchMin..MatchMax.

nodes.name: UpdateState
nodes.summary: Recomputes whether the current count is inside the match range and fires the count, match and unmatch events on transitions.

nodes.name: LeanDropCount_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector for LeanDropCount exposing the count, match range and the three event groups.

nodes.name: LeanFingerDownCanvas.cs
nodes.summary: UI variant of the external LeanFingerDown component that only reacts to fingers pressing the Canvas element it is attached to.
nodes.languageNotes: Requires the UI graphic's RaycastTarget setting; the Canvas suffix convention throughout this package means 'raycast against UI instead of world colliders'.

nodes.name: LeanFingerDownCanvas
nodes.summary: Subclass of the external LeanFingerDown that overrides HandleFingerDown to ignore fingers whose press did not land on this RectTransform.

nodes.name: LeanFingerDownCanvas_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanFingerDownCanvas, extending the external LeanFingerDown_Editor.

nodes.name: LeanFingerFlick.cs
nodes.summary: Swipe detector that fires while the finger is still touching the screen, rather than waiting for release, plus its inspector editor.

nodes.name: LeanFingerFlick
nodes.summary: LeanSwipeBase subclass that tracks each finger in a nested FingerData list and, per frame, tests the recorded movement against the Check mode (CheckType enum) to raise a swipe mid-touch.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Walks the tracked fingers each frame, building the from/to screen positions for the configured check mode and testing them for a flick.

nodes.name: TestFinger
nodes.summary: Applies the GUI and required-selectable filters, then delegates to LeanSwipeBase to evaluate and dispatch the swipe between the two screen points.

nodes.name: LeanFingerFlick_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanFingerFlick extending LeanSwipeBase_Editor with the GUI-ignore and check-mode fields.

nodes.name: LeanFingerHeld.cs
nodes.summary: Core hold-detection component: fires down/update/up events once a finger has stayed on the screen for MinimumAge without moving more than MaximumMovement. Base class for the Canvas variant.

nodes.name: LeanFingerHeld
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour that keeps a nested FingerData entry per touching finger, decides when the hold conditions are met, and invokes both finger-space and world-space UnityEvents for the down, update and up phases.
nodes.languageNotes: Exposes parallel OnFinger*/OnWorld* event sets, so designers can consume either the raw finger or a ScreenDepth-projected world position.

nodes.name: HandleFingerDown
nodes.summary: Starts tracking a new finger after the GUI and required-selectable filters pass, allocating its FingerData state.

nodes.name: HandleFingerUpdate
nodes.summary: Per-finger state machine: evaluates the hold conditions each update and drives the transitions that invoke the down, update and up events, discarding fingers that moved too far.

nodes.name: LeanFingerHeld_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanFingerHeld drawing the age/movement thresholds and conditionally showing the world-space event group; also the base editor for the Canvas variant.

nodes.name: LeanFingerHeldCanvas.cs
nodes.summary: UI variant of LeanFingerHeld that only detects holds on the Canvas element it is attached to.

nodes.name: LeanFingerHeldCanvas
nodes.summary: Subclass of LeanFingerHeld overriding HandleFingerDown so only fingers pressing this UI element are tracked.

nodes.name: LeanFingerHeldCanvas_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanFingerHeldCanvas, reusing LeanFingerHeld_Editor's drawing.

nodes.name: LeanFingerTapExpired.cs
nodes.summary: Tap component that only fires once the tap counter has expired, which is how single and double taps are told apart without interfering.
nodes.languageNotes: Expiry timing comes from the global LeanTouch.TapThreshold setting rather than a local field.

nodes.name: LeanFingerTapExpired
nodes.summary: Subclass of the external LeanFingerTap that subscribes to the finger-expired event instead of the tap event, so the final tap count is known before the events fire.

nodes.name: LeanFingerTapExpired_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanFingerTapExpired, extending the external LeanFingerTap_Editor.

nodes.name: LeanFingerTapQuick.cs
nodes.summary: Detects the final tap of a multi-tap sequence at the moment the finger touches down, giving instant response for the last tap only.

nodes.name: LeanFingerTapQuick
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour that listens for finger-down and fires its finger, world and screen UnityEvents as soon as the running tap count reaches RequiredTapCount.

nodes.name: HandleFingerDown
nodes.summary: Applies the GUI and selectable filters, compares the finger's tap count with RequiredTapCount, and invokes the finger, world and screen events.

nodes.name: LeanFingerTapQuick_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanFingerTapQuick drawing the tap-count requirement and the three event groups.

nodes.name: LeanFirstDown.cs
nodes.summary: Fires events only when the first finger begins touching the screen, ignoring additional simultaneous fingers. Base class for the Canvas variant.

nodes.name: LeanFirstDown
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour that keeps a list of active fingers and raises its finger, world and screen events only for the transition from zero to one touching finger; UseFinger is the virtual hook the Canvas variant overrides.

nodes.name: UseFinger
nodes.summary: Virtual filter deciding whether a finger counts toward the first-down detection; overridden by the Canvas subclass to require a UI hit.

nodes.name: HandleFingerDown
nodes.summary: Adds the finger to the tracked list and, when it is the first one, invokes the finger, world and screen UnityEvents.

nodes.name: LeanFirstDown_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanFirstDown and base editor for the Canvas variant, drawing the filters and event groups.

nodes.name: LeanFirstDownCanvas.cs
nodes.summary: UI variant of LeanFirstDown that only counts fingers pressing the Canvas element it is attached to.

nodes.name: LeanFirstDownCanvas
nodes.summary: Subclass of LeanFirstDown that overrides UseFinger to require the finger to be over this UI element.

nodes.name: LeanFirstDownCanvas_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanFirstDownCanvas, reusing LeanFirstDown_Editor's drawing.

nodes.name: LeanGestureToggle.cs
nodes.summary: Arbitrates between drag, pinch and twist components by enabling only the one whose gesture exceeded its threshold first, the way mobile map apps isolate gestures.

nodes.name: LeanGestureToggle
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour that accumulates the filtered fingers' drag, pinch and twist magnitudes each frame and, once one crosses its threshold, switches the StateType state so only that component stays enabled.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Per-frame arbitration: accumulates delta, scale and twist from the active fingers, picks the winning gesture against its threshold, and enables or disables the target components accordingly.

nodes.name: LeanGestureToggle_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanGestureToggle exposing the three target components and their thresholds.

nodes.name: LeanLastUp.cs
nodes.summary: Fires events when the last finger stops touching the screen, the release-side counterpart to LeanFirstDown. Base class for the Canvas variant.

nodes.name: LeanLastUp
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour that tracks touching fingers and raises its finger, world and screen events only when the tracked list empties.

nodes.name: HandleFingerDown
nodes.summary: Registers a finger in the tracked list once the GUI and required-selectable filters pass.

nodes.name: HandleFingerUp
nodes.summary: Removes the finger and, when none remain, invokes the finger, world and screen UnityEvents for the last-up moment.

nodes.name: LeanLastUp_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanLastUp and base editor for the Canvas variant.

nodes.name: LeanLastUpCanvas.cs
nodes.summary: UI variant of LeanLastUp that only tracks fingers which started on the Canvas element it is attached to.

nodes.name: LeanLastUpCanvas
nodes.summary: Subclass of LeanLastUp overriding HandleFingerDown so only fingers over this UI element are counted toward the last-up event.

nodes.name: LeanLastUpCanvas_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanLastUpCanvas, reusing LeanLastUp_Editor's drawing.

nodes.name: LeanManualFlick.cs
nodes.summary: Swipe detector whose fingers are fed in manually via AddFinger by components such as LeanFingerDown or LeanFingerDownCanvas, so a flick can be scoped to a specific object or UI element.

nodes.name: LeanManualFlick
nodes.summary: LeanSwipeBase subclass with a public AddFinger/RemoveFinger API and a nested FingerData list; each frame it tests the tracked fingers against the Check mode and dispatches swipe events.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Iterates the manually added fingers, resolving the from/to screen positions for the configured check mode and testing each for a flick.

nodes.name: TestFinger
nodes.summary: Applies the GUI and required-selectable filters, then hands the two screen points to LeanSwipeBase for swipe evaluation.

nodes.name: LeanManualFlick_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanManualFlick extending LeanSwipeBase_Editor.

nodes.name: LeanManualSwipe.cs
nodes.summary: Swipe-detection component that only reacts to fingers explicitly handed to it, so a swipe can be scoped to fingers registered by another component such as LeanFingerDown or LeanFingerDownCanvas.
nodes.languageNotes: Derives from the external LeanSwipeBase, which supplies the OnSwipe UnityEvent surface; this class only decides which fingers qualify.

nodes.name: LeanManualSwipe
nodes.summary: Tracks a manually populated finger list and forwards LeanTouch.OnFingerSwipe to the inherited swipe events, optionally gated on a required LeanSelectable being selected.

nodes.name: LeanManualSwipe_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanManualSwipe, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: AddFinger
nodes.summary: Registers a finger for swipe tracking, lazily creating the list and de-duplicating existing entries.

nodes.name: HandleFingerSwipe
nodes.summary: LeanTouch swipe callback that only fires for manually added fingers, skipping fingers over GUI or when the required selectable is not selected.

nodes.name: LeanMouseWheel.cs
nodes.summary: Turns mouse wheel scrolling into a float UnityEvent so wheel input can drive other components (zoom, scale, dial) without custom code.

nodes.name: LeanMouseWheel
nodes.summary: Polls CwInput for wheel delta each frame, optionally gated on a selected LeanSelectable and a held mouse button, then transforms the delta (sign, multiplier, one-based) and invokes OnDelta.

nodes.name: LeanMouseWheel_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanMouseWheel, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: ModifyType
nodes.summary: Selects whether the raw wheel delta is used as-is or reduced to its sign.

nodes.name: CoordinateType
nodes.summary: Selects whether the emitted delta is zero-based or shifted to be one-based (useful for multiplicative zoom).

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Per-frame wheel poll: applies the selectable and mouse-button gates, reads CwInput.GetMouseWheelDelta, applies ModifyType/multiplier/CoordinateType, and invokes OnDelta.

nodes.name: LeanMultiDirection.cs
nodes.summary: Measures how far one or more filtered fingers have moved along a configured screen direction and emits that distance as a float event.

nodes.name: LeanMultiDirection
nodes.summary: Uses a LeanFingerFilter to gather fingers each frame, projects their combined screen movement onto a configured direction, converts it via CoordinateType, and invokes the distance event.

nodes.name: LeanMultiDirection_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanMultiDirection, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: CoordinateType
nodes.summary: Chooses the unit the emitted distance is reported in (raw pixels, scaled pixels, or screen percentage).

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Gathers filtered fingers, computes movement along the configured direction, scales it by CoordinateType and the multiplier, and invokes the event unless movement is zero and ignored.

nodes.name: LeanMultiDown.cs
nodes.summary: Fires UnityEvents the moment a specific number of fingers are simultaneously pressing the screen, reporting the finger list plus the screen and world center.

nodes.name: LeanMultiDown
nodes.summary: Subscribes to LeanTouch.OnFingerDown/OnFingerUp, maintains the set of currently pressing fingers, and invokes the finger-list, screen-center, and world-position events once the required count is reached.

nodes.name: LeanMultiDown_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanMultiDown, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: HandleFingerDown
nodes.summary: Filters out GUI-started and hover fingers, adds the finger to the tracked set, and when the required finger count is met invokes the finger-list, screen-center, and converted world-position events.

nodes.name: LeanMultiHeld.cs
nodes.summary: Detects a sustained multi-finger hold: once the required fingers have stayed down past a minimum age (within a movement tolerance) it fires down/update/up event triples for finger list, screen center, and world position.
nodes.languageNotes: Nests a private FingerData : LeanFingerData subclass so accumulated per-finger movement can be tracked through LeanFingerData.FindOrCreate.

nodes.name: LeanMultiHeld
nodes.summary: Tracks per-finger accumulated movement via LeanFingerData, accumulates hold duration in the OnGesture callback, and drives the three-phase (down/update/up) event set once the hold conditions hold true.

nodes.name: LeanMultiHeld_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanMultiHeld, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: HandleFingerDown
nodes.summary: Rejects GUI-started and hover fingers, then creates/resets the FingerData movement accumulator and tracks the finger.

nodes.name: HandleGesture
nodes.summary: Per-gesture tick that accumulates each finger's scaled delta, prunes released fingers, then advances the hold duration and fires InvokeDown/InvokeUpdate/InvokeUp as the held state changes.

nodes.name: InvokeDown
nodes.summary: Fires the hold-begin events: the finger list, the screen center, and that center converted to a world position via ScreenDepth.

nodes.name: InvokeUpdate
nodes.summary: Fires the per-frame hold events with the current finger list, screen center, and converted world position.

nodes.name: InvokeUp
nodes.summary: Fires the hold-end events with the final finger list, screen center, and converted world position.

nodes.name: LeanMultiPinch.cs
nodes.summary: Reports the pinch (scale) ratio of all filtered fingers as a float event, letting designers wire pinch straight into scale or zoom.

nodes.name: LeanMultiPinch
nodes.summary: Gathers fingers through a LeanFingerFilter each frame and emits the LeanGesture pinch ratio, converted by CoordinateType and scaled by the multiplier, optionally skipping frames with no pinching.

nodes.name: LeanMultiPinch_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanMultiPinch, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: CoordinateType
nodes.summary: Chooses how the pinch value is expressed (e.g. ratio versus a delta form) before it is emitted.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Per-frame pinch calculation: pulls the filtered fingers, derives the pinch ratio/scale from LeanGesture, converts it per CoordinateType, and invokes the float event.

nodes.name: LeanMultiPull.cs
nodes.summary: Continuously reports where the filtered fingers are relative to where they first went down, which is what an invisible on-screen joystick needs.

nodes.name: LeanMultiPull
nodes.summary: Each frame compares the current finger center against the start center and emits the offset as distance, screen delta, and world from/to events - effectively a virtual joystick driver.

nodes.name: LeanMultiPull_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanMultiPull, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: CoordinateType
nodes.summary: Chooses the unit for the emitted pull offset (raw pixels, scaled pixels, or screen percentage).

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Computes the start-to-current finger center offset, applies CoordinateType scaling and the multiplier, and invokes the distance, delta, and world position events.

nodes.name: LeanMultiSwipe.cs
nodes.summary: Detects a simultaneous multi-finger swipe, distinguishing a parallel swipe from a pinch-in or pinch-out swipe, and fires when the first finger leaves the screen.

nodes.name: LeanMultiSwipe
nodes.summary: Watches the filtered finger set for the first swiping finger, then validates every finger against age and distance thresholds and classifies the result as parallel, swipe-in, or swipe-out.

nodes.name: LeanMultiSwipe_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanMultiSwipe, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Scans the filtered fingers for the first one flagged as swiped, delegates to FingerSwipe once per gesture, and resets the latch when no fingers remain.

nodes.name: FingerSwipe
nodes.summary: Validates every finger against the tap-age and scaled-distance thresholds, measures pairwise angles to decide if the swipe is parallel, and otherwise emits swipe-in/swipe-out based on the pinch distance change.

nodes.name: LeanMultiTap.cs
nodes.summary: Counts multi-taps - one or more fingers pressed and released together within the tap threshold - and reports the tap count and the highest simultaneous finger count.

nodes.name: LeanMultiTap
nodes.summary: Tracks how many filtered fingers are still down each frame, ages the current tap window, and on full release increments the multi-tap count and fires the tap/count/highest events.

nodes.name: LeanMultiTap_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanMultiTap, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Ages the tap window, records the peak simultaneous finger count, and on full release within LeanTouch.CurrentTapThreshold increments the multi-tap count and invokes the tap, count, highest, and combined events; resets once the window expires.

nodes.name: GetFingerCount
nodes.summary: Counts how many of the supplied fingers are still touching the screen (not flagged Up).

nodes.name: LeanMultiTwist.cs
nodes.summary: Reports the twist (rotation) angle of all filtered fingers as a float event, with a configurable fallback for how a single finger is interpreted.
nodes.languageNotes: The editor class in this file is misnamed LeanDestroy_Editor - a copy-paste leftover from another component, recorded here rather than normalized.

nodes.name: LeanMultiTwist
nodes.summary: Gathers fingers via a LeanFingerFilter and emits the LeanGesture twist degrees each frame, with OneFingerType deciding how a lone finger is treated and an option to skip zero-twist frames.

nodes.name: LeanDestroy_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanMultiTwist. NOTE: the class is misnamed LeanDestroy_Editor (copy-paste leftover); it targets LeanMultiTwist via the TARGET alias, so behaviour is correct but the name is misleading.

nodes.name: OneFingerType
nodes.summary: Decides how a single finger is interpreted for twist (ignored, or twisted around a reference point).

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Pulls the filtered fingers, computes the twist degrees from LeanGesture, applies the OneFingerType rule and multiplier, and invokes the float event.

nodes.name: LeanMultiUp.cs
nodes.summary: Fires UnityEvents when a specific number of fingers stop touching the screen, reporting the releasing finger plus the screen and world position.

nodes.name: LeanMultiUp
nodes.summary: Monitors the filtered finger set each frame and, when the required count is released, invokes the finger, screen-position, and converted world-position events.

nodes.name: LeanMultiUp_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanMultiUp, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Watches the filtered fingers for the release condition and invokes the finger, screen, and world events once the required number of fingers has lifted.

nodes.name: LeanMultiUpdate.cs
nodes.summary: The general-purpose workhorse of the LeanMulti family: reports the per-frame change in position of all filtered fingers as delta, distance, and world from/to events, with optional axis constraining.
nodes.languageNotes: Its GetFingers and HandleFingerDown are virtual specifically so LeanMultiUpdateCanvas can narrow the finger set to a UI element.

nodes.name: LeanMultiUpdate
nodes.summary: Computes the finger-center delta each frame, optionally locks movement to the dominant axis once a cumulative threshold is passed, and emits the finger list, delta, distance, and world from/to/delta events.

nodes.name: LeanMultiUpdate_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanMultiUpdate, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: CoordinateType
nodes.summary: Chooses the unit the emitted delta is expressed in (raw pixels, scaled pixels, or screen percentage).

nodes.name: ConstrainType
nodes.summary: Selects whether movement is free or locked to the dominant horizontal/vertical axis once a threshold is crossed, and how the pre-threshold movement is handled.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Core gesture tick: derives the last-to-current finger center delta, applies the ConstrainType axis locking against a cumulative threshold, scales by CoordinateType and multiplier, then invokes the finger, delta, distance, and world from/to/delta events.

nodes.name: GetFingers
nodes.summary: Virtual finger-source hook returning the filter's current fingers; overridden by LeanMultiUpdateCanvas to restrict the set to a UI element.

nodes.name: HandleFingerDown
nodes.summary: Virtual finger-down hook that ignores the hover finger and registers the rest with the filter; overridden to add a UI overlap test.

nodes.name: LeanMultiUpdateCanvas.cs
nodes.summary: Canvas variant of LeanMultiUpdate that only counts fingers currently overlapping this UI element, so drag-style events fire for the RectTransform rather than the whole screen.
nodes.languageNotes: Follows the package-wide *Canvas convention: identical behaviour to the base component, but raycasting against Canvas/UI elements instead of world colliders.

nodes.name: LeanMultiUpdateCanvas
nodes.summary: Overrides GetFingers to drop fingers not overlapping this UI element and HandleFingerDown to only accept presses that started on it, inheriting all delta/world event logic from LeanMultiUpdate.

nodes.name: LeanMultiUpdateCanvas_Editor
nodes.summary: Inspector for LeanMultiUpdateCanvas that extends LeanMultiUpdate_Editor and adds the IgnoreIfOff field.

nodes.name: GetFingers
nodes.summary: Takes the base finger set and removes any finger whose current screen position is not over this UI element, tested with LeanTouch.ElementOverlapped.

nodes.name: HandleFingerDown
nodes.summary: Only forwards finger-down to the base implementation when the press lands on this UI element.

nodes.name: LeanPick.cs
nodes.summary: Scene-level picker that raycasts a screen position for a LeanPickable and notifies it, providing a lightweight alternative to the full LeanSelectable selection system.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately requires an external caller (e.g. LeanFingerTap wired in the Inspector) - it subscribes to nothing itself.

nodes.name: LeanPick
nodes.summary: Queries the screen position via ScreenQuery for a LeanPickable, optionally filtered by a required tag, then invokes OnPickable and calls the target's InvokePick.

nodes.name: LeanPick_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanPick, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: SelectScreenPosition
nodes.summary: Runs a ScreenQuery for a LeanPickable at the given screen position, discards results whose tag does not match RequiredTag, then invokes OnPickable and forwards to LeanPickable.InvokePick.

nodes.name: LeanPickable.cs
nodes.summary: Marker component making a GameObject pickable by LeanPick, exposing finger, screen-position, and world-position events when it is picked.
nodes.languageNotes: The editor class in this file is misnamed LeanSelectSelf_Editor - an orphaned remnant of the now-emptied LeanSelectSelf.cs, recorded here rather than normalized.

nodes.name: LeanPickable
nodes.summary: Holds the OnFinger/OnWorld/OnScreen UnityEvents that LeanPick fires when this GameObject is picked; contains no input logic of its own.

nodes.name: LeanSelectSelf_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanPickable. NOTE: the class is misnamed LeanSelectSelf_Editor - an orphaned leftover from LeanSelectSelf.cs (now an empty stub); it targets LeanPickable via the TARGET alias.

nodes.name: InvokePick
nodes.summary: Called by LeanPick to fire the finger event, the screen position event, and the ScreenDepth-converted world position event.

nodes.name: LeanPinchCamera.cs
nodes.summary: Zooms a camera from the pinch gesture, handling both orthographic size and perspective field-of-view, with damping, clamping, and optional zoom-toward-the-pinch-point behaviour.
nodes.languageNotes: Zoom writes to orthographicSize or fieldOfView depending on the camera projection, and relative zoom shifts the transform so the pinch point stays put.

nodes.name: LeanPinchCamera
nodes.summary: Tracks a target zoom plus a damped current zoom, applies the LeanGesture pinch ratio in LateUpdate, optionally translates the camera so the pinch center stays fixed, and writes the result to the camera.

nodes.name: LeanPinchCamera_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanPinchCamera, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: ContinuouslyZoom
nodes.summary: Public hook that lerps zoom toward the clamp max or min based on the sign of the supplied direction, for held-button style continuous zooming.

nodes.name: IncrementZoom
nodes.summary: Converts a signed delta into a multiplicative factor (0 = no change, -1 halves, 2 doubles) and applies it through MultiplyZoom.

nodes.name: LateUpdate
nodes.summary: Applies the pinch ratio to the clamped zoom, and when Relative is set repositions the transform so the pinch screen center stays anchored, then damps both current zoom and the remaining translation before writing the camera value.

nodes.name: SetZoom
nodes.summary: Writes the zoom value to the resolved camera as orthographicSize or fieldOfView depending on projection, logging an error when no camera can be found.

nodes.name: LeanReplayFinger.cs
nodes.summary: Demonstration component that records the last finger stroke from LeanTouch snapshots and can replay it, moving a cursor Transform along the recorded path.

nodes.name: LeanReplayFinger
nodes.summary: Copies a finger's LeanSnapshot history on finger-up and, when Replay is called, advances a play time and moves the cursor to the interpolated recorded screen position converted through ScreenDepth.

nodes.name: LeanReplayFinger_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanReplayFinger, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: While playing, advances play time and moves the cursor to the snapshot-interpolated screen position converted to world space.

nodes.name: HandleFingerUpdate
nodes.summary: Live finger callback that cancels playback and drives the cursor directly from the current finger position, skipping GUI-started fingers.

nodes.name: CopySnapshots
nodes.summary: Deep-copies the finger's snapshot list (age plus screen position) into a locally owned list, since LeanTouch recycles its snapshots.

nodes.name: LeanSelectSelf.cs
nodes.summary: Emptied-out placeholder: the file contains only a UTF-8 BOM and a "// Remove" comment, with no code at all. Its former editor class survives as the misnamed LeanSelectSelf_Editor inside LeanPickable.cs.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableBlock.cs
nodes.summary: Reference implementation of a match-3 style grid block: it holds integer grid coordinates, swaps with the neighbouring block the selecting finger drags toward, and eases into its grid position.
nodes.languageNotes: Keeps a static Instances list registered in OnEnable/OnDisable, so FindBlock is an O(n) linear scan over all live blocks rather than a grid lookup.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableBlock
nodes.summary: A selectable grid block tracking x/y coordinates in a static instance registry; while selected it converts the finger position to a grid coordinate and swaps with an adjacent block, then damps its transform toward the target grid position.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableBlock_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanSelectableBlock, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: FindBlock
nodes.summary: Static linear scan over the Instances registry returning the block at the given x/y grid coordinate, or null.

nodes.name: Swap
nodes.summary: Static helper exchanging the x/y grid coordinates of two blocks; the damped Update then animates both into their new positions.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: While selected, projects the selecting finger to a world point at the block's depth, rounds it to a grid coordinate, and if that coordinate is orthogonally adjacent swaps with the block found there (optionally deselecting); then damps localPosition toward x/y * BlockSize.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableCenter.cs
nodes.summary: On demand, averages the world positions of every currently selected LeanSelectable and emits the centroid as a Vector3 event.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableCenter
nodes.summary: Exposes a Calculate method (also a context-menu item) that averages the transform positions of all selected LeanSelectable instances and invokes OnPosition; it does nothing on its own each frame.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableCenter_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanSelectableCenter, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: Calculate
nodes.summary: Iterates LeanSelectable.Instances, sums the positions of the selected ones, and invokes OnPosition with the average when at least one is selected.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableDial.cs
nodes.summary: Turns the selected object into a dial or knob: dragging rotates it about a configured axis, with optional angle clamping and a list of angular triggers that fire enter/exit events.
nodes.languageNotes: GetPoint has two paths - RectTransformUtility for a Canvas dial (overlay and camera render modes handled separately) and a plane raycast for a world-space dial.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableDial
nodes.summary: Accumulates the signed angle swept by the selecting finger around the dial axis, clamps it if configured, applies it as a local rotation on top of a tilt, and drives the angular Trigger enter/exit events.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableDial_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanSelectableDial, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: Trigger
nodes.summary: Serializable angular zone with min/max bounds, an inside latch, and OnEnter/OnExit UnityEvents fired as the dial angle crosses into or out of the zone.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Resets to the tilt orientation, measures the signed angle between the previous and current finger points around the axis, applies clamping, rotates the transform, then evaluates every Trigger and fires its OnEnter/OnExit on state change.

nodes.name: GetPoint
nodes.summary: Converts a screen position into a dial-local 2D point: via RectTransformUtility when on a Canvas (handling overlay versus camera render modes) or via a plane raycast against the dial axis for world objects, falling back to the previous point.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableDragTorque.cs
nodes.summary: Adds physics torque to the attached Rigidbody based on how the selecting finger spins, so a selected object can be flicked into rotation.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableDragTorque
nodes.summary: While selected, compares the previous and current finger deltas to derive an angular change and applies it as torque about the camera forward axis on the cached Rigidbody.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableDragTorque_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanSelectableDragTorque, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Derives the angle between the previous and current finger scaled deltas, weights it by their combined magnitude, and applies the result as an acceleration-mode torque about the camera forward axis; logs an error when no camera resolves.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableDrop.cs
nodes.summary: On finger release, raycasts under the selected object for an IDropHandler and hands the drop over to it, emitting the receiving GameObject and handler as events.
nodes.languageNotes: Temporarily moves this GameObject (and optionally its ancestors) to IgnoreRaycast via LeanScreenQuery.ChangeLayers so the query can see through the dragged object.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableDrop
nodes.summary: Handles the select-finger-up event by querying the screen position for an IDropHandler - masking its own layers first - then calls HandleDrop on the target and invokes the GameObject and handler events.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableDrop_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanSelectableDrop, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: IgnoreType
nodes.summary: Selects whether this GameObject alone, this GameObject plus its ancestors, or nothing is temporarily switched to IgnoreRaycast during the drop query.

nodes.name: OnSelectedSelectFingerUp
nodes.summary: On finger release, masks layers per IgnoreType, runs ScreenQuery.TryQuery for an IDropHandler, reverts the layers, then calls HandleDrop and invokes the GameObject and handler events on success.

nodes.name: LeanSelectablePressureScale.cs
nodes.summary: Scales the selected object in proportion to the selecting finger pressure, for force-touch style feedback.

nodes.name: LeanSelectablePressureScale
nodes.summary: Reads the selecting finger's Pressure each frame, optionally clamps it to 0..1, and sets localScale to BaseScale plus a pressure-weighted multiple of it.

nodes.name: LeanSelectablePressureScale_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanSelectablePressureScale, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Samples the selecting finger pressure (0 when nothing is selected), optionally clamps it, and writes localScale = baseScale + baseScale * pressure * multiplier.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableSelected.cs
nodes.summary: Fires down/update/up events once a selectable has been held selected for a threshold number of seconds, with configurable reset timing and an optional require-a-finger gate.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableSelected
nodes.summary: Accumulates selected time each frame, and once past the threshold fires the down event on the first qualifying frame, the update event every frame after, and the up event on deselect; ResetType controls when the timer clears.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableSelected_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom Unity inspector for LeanSelectableSelected, drawing its serialized fields and surfacing setup warnings in the Inspector.

nodes.name: ResetType
nodes.summary: Selects whether the accumulated seconds are cleared on select, on deselect, or not at all.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Increments the selected-seconds timer while selected (optionally requiring a selecting finger via LeanSelectableByFinger), then fires the down event on the first frame past the threshold and the update event every frame thereafter.

nodes.name: OnSelected
nodes.summary: Clears the timer when ResetType is OnSelect and resets the latch so the down event can fire again.

nodes.name: OnDeselected
nodes.summary: Clears the timer when ResetType is OnDeselect and fires the up event if the threshold had been reached.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Unity Package Manager manifest for com.cwilkes.lean.touch-plus (v1.0.0, Unity 2019.4+), declaring runtime dependencies on the com.cwilkes.lean.common and com.cwilkes.lean.common-plus packages.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableTime.cs
nodes.summary: Defines a LeanSelectable companion component that accumulates how many seconds an object has been selected and broadcasts the running total through a UnityEvent, with a SendType switch controlling whether it fires only while selected, also on deselect, or every frame.
nodes.languageNotes: The sibling inspector class in the #if UNITY_EDITOR block is misnamed LeanPlane_Editor, an apparent copy-paste leftover from an unrelated component.

nodes.name: LeanSelectableTime
nodes.summary: LeanSelectableBehaviour subclass that counts elapsed selected time in Update and invokes a float UnityEvent with the running seconds, resetting to zero once the object is deselected.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Per-frame tick that adds deltaTime while the Selectable is selected, zeroes the counter on deselect, and decides whether to invoke the OnSeconds event based on the configured SendType.

nodes.name: LeanPlane_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector drawing the Send and OnSeconds fields for LeanSelectableTime. ANOMALY: the class is named LeanPlane_Editor rather than LeanSelectableTime_Editor, a copy-paste leftover from an unrelated component; the name is recorded as it actually appears in the source.

nodes.name: LeanSelectionBox.cs
nodes.summary: Implements drag-rectangle multi-selection: each finger spawns a RectTransform selection box prefab under a screen-filling canvas root, the box is resized as the finger drags, and on release every LeanSelectable inside the rectangle passing the layer and tag filters is handed to a LeanSelectByFinger component.

nodes.name: LeanSelectionBox
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour that tracks per-finger FingerData entries mapping a finger to its spawned selection-box RectTransform, updates the box geometry each frame, and resolves the enclosed selectables on finger release.

nodes.name: HandleFingerDown
nodes.summary: Starts a new selection box for a finger, skipping fingers that began over GUI, instantiating the prefab under the canvas root and registering the finger's FingerData.

nodes.name: HandleFingerSet
nodes.summary: Updates the live selection box rectangle for a moving finger by re-writing its RectTransform each frame.

nodes.name: HandleFingerUp
nodes.summary: Finalizes a selection box on finger release: collects the selectables it encloses, passes them to the configured select component, then destroys the box and recycles the FingerData.

nodes.name: WriteTransform
nodes.summary: Core geometry routine converting the finger's start and current screen positions into the selection box's anchored rect, and testing every LeanSelectable's screen-projected position against that rect and the layer filter.

nodes.name: HasRequiredTag
nodes.summary: Returns whether a candidate tag matches the RequiredTags allow-list, treating an empty list as accept-everything.

nodes.name: LeanSelectionBox_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector for LeanSelectionBox that draws the camera, prefab, root, select target and layer/tag filter fields with validation warnings for missing references.

nodes.name: LeanShape.cs
nodes.summary: Defines a reusable 2D gesture shape as an ordered list of Vector2 points, optionally closed into a loop, with index wrapping/clamping accessors and optional LineRenderer visualisation. This is the reference data that LeanShapeDetector matches finger movement against.

nodes.name: LeanShape
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour holding the point list that describes a gesture shape, exposing ConnectEnds looping, a static positive-modulo helper, indexed point lookup with optional reversal, and LineRenderer sync.

nodes.name: GetPoint
nodes.summary: Returns the shape point at an index, optionally traversing in reverse, wrapping the index when ConnectEnds is set and clamping it otherwise.

nodes.name: UpdateVisual
nodes.summary: Pushes the current point list into the assigned LineRenderer, appending a duplicate of the first point when the shape is a closed loop.

nodes.name: LeanShape_Editor
nodes.summary: Large custom inspector for LeanShape providing interactive scene-view point editing, add/remove/drag handling and visual refresh — the bulk of the file's line count.

nodes.name: LeanShapeDetector.cs
nodes.summary: The package's gesture-recognition core: records each finger's stroke as a decimated point list and, on release, matches it against a reference LeanShape using point-to-segment distance with configurable distance/error thresholds, partial-match minimums and forward/backward direction ranges, firing OnDetected on a match.
nodes.languageNotes: Pools FingerData instances in a static Stack and reuses static scratch collections (ranges, fittedShape, referenceLines) to avoid per-frame GC allocations — a common Unity mobile optimisation.

nodes.name: LeanShapeDetector
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour that consumes a LeanShape reference, accumulates per-finger drawn points above a step threshold, and runs the shape-matching pipeline (range enumeration, CalculateMatch, FitShape) to detect gestures.

nodes.name: Line
nodes.summary: Private struct representing a reference shape segment, providing point-to-endpoint and point-to-segment distance maths used by the matching algorithm.

nodes.name: HandleFingerDown
nodes.summary: Begins tracking a new finger stroke by pulling a pooled FingerData, clearing its point list and seeding it with the finger's starting position.

nodes.name: HandleFingerUp
nodes.summary: Runs the match on finger release: builds the candidate index ranges from the reference shape (honouring ConnectEnds and MinimumPoints), calls CalculateMatch for each, and invokes OnDetected on the first success before recycling the FingerData.

nodes.name: AddRange
nodes.summary: Appends forward and/or reversed index ranges to the shared ranges list according to the configured DirectionType, so a shape can be matched drawn either way.

nodes.name: CalculateMatch
nodes.summary: The matching kernel: walks the drawn point queue against the reference line queue, accumulating an error factor whenever a point strays beyond the distance threshold and failing the match once the error exceeds the allowance.

nodes.name: FitShape
nodes.summary: Normalises the drawn stroke into the reference shape's local space by comparing bounding rects, so matching is scale and position independent.

nodes.name: ConvertPoints
nodes.summary: Turns the selected index range of the reference shape's points into the queue of Line segments the matcher consumes, handling reversed ranges.

nodes.name: GetRect
nodes.summary: Computes the axis-aligned bounding rect of a point list, used by FitShape to align drawn and reference shapes.

nodes.name: LeanShapeDetector_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector exposing the detector's shape reference and the step, distance, error and minimum-point thresholds with explanatory tooltips.

nodes.name: LeanSpawnWithFinger.cs
nodes.summary: Spawns a prefab at a finger's world position derived from a LeanScreenDepth conversion, optionally keeping it dragging under the finger, auto-selecting it via LeanSelect, and destroying it on release when dropped over blocked or missing screen-query targets.
nodes.languageNotes: Spawn must be called externally (e.g. from a UnityEvent) rather than being triggered internally, making this a designer-wired factory component.

nodes.name: LeanSpawnWithFinger
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour factory that instantiates a Transform prefab under a finger, tracks the clone and its optional LeanSelectable in pooled FingerData, and applies pixel/world offsets plus rotation modes each frame while the finger is held.

nodes.name: Spawn
nodes.summary: Public entry point that instantiates the prefab at the finger, positions and rotates it per the ScreenDepth and RotateType settings, optionally selects it and registers a pooled FingerData when DragAfterSpawn is enabled.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Per-frame pass that re-positions every still-held clone by delegating to UpdateSpawnedTransform.

nodes.name: UpdateSpawnedTransform
nodes.summary: Converts the finger's screen position (with pixel offset scaled by an optional Canvas) into a world position, applies the world offset relative to an optional Transform, and sets the clone's rotation from the chosen RotateType.

nodes.name: HandleFingerUp
nodes.summary: On release, runs the blocked and missing screen queries to decide whether to destroy the clone, deselects it when configured, and returns the FingerData to the pool.

nodes.name: LeanSpawnWithFinger_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector for LeanSpawnWithFinger, conditionally revealing the screen-query, selection and offset field groups based on the enabled toggles.

nodes.name: LeanSwipeEdge.cs
nodes.summary: Detects swipes that originate at a screen edge, checking the swipe start against a scaled-pixel edge threshold and its direction against an angle tolerance for each enabled side, then firing a UnityEvent.

nodes.name: LeanSwipeEdge
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour with per-side Left/Right/Bottom/Top toggles, angle and edge thresholds, and a LeanFingerFilter, exposing both automatic Update-driven detection and a manual CheckBetween entry point.

nodes.name: CheckBetween
nodes.summary: Manual entry point that tests a from/to screen vector against each enabled edge, requiring both the start point to be near that edge and the direction to fall within the angle threshold.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Pulls the filtered fingers each frame and forwards any that just swiped to CheckBetween using their start and current screen positions.

nodes.name: LeanSwipeEdge_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector drawing the edge toggles, thresholds and OnEdge event for LeanSwipeEdge, warning when no edge is enabled.

nodes.name: LeanTwistCamera.cs
nodes.summary: Rotates the attached GameObject (typically a camera) from a two-finger twist gesture, optionally pivoting around the finger centre in world space via LeanScreenDepth, with damped interpolation toward the target rotation.
nodes.languageNotes: Keeps remainingTranslation/remainingRotation as serialized leftovers and consumes a fraction each frame, the standard Lean Touch damping idiom for frame-rate independent smoothing.

nodes.name: LeanTwistCamera
nodes.summary: MonoBehaviour applying twist-gesture rotation with a LeanFingerFilter, a Damping factor, and a Relative mode that rotates about the finger centre rather than the transform origin.

nodes.name: Update
nodes.summary: Reads the twist degrees from the filtered fingers, accumulates the pending rotation and (in Relative mode) the pivot translation, then applies a damped fraction of both to the transform each frame.

nodes.name: LeanTwistCamera_Editor
nodes.summary: Custom inspector drawing the finger filter, damping and relative settings for LeanTwistCamera.

edges.description: LeanDragTranslateAlongRigidbody.cs:9 subclasses LeanDragTranslateAlong (and :73 subclasses its editor).
LeanFingerHeldCanvas.cs:8 subclasses LeanFingerHeld (and :35 subclasses its editor).
LeanFirstDownCanvas.cs:9 subclasses LeanFirstDown (and :33 subclasses its editor).
LeanLastUpCanvas.cs:10 subclasses LeanLastUp (and :37 subclasses its editor).
LeanSelectableDrop.cs:21 declares UnityEvent<IDropHandler> and :46 resolves an IDropHandler to invoke HandleDrop on.
LeanManualSwipe.cs:7 documents LeanFingerDownCanvas as a source of manually-added fingers. Inspector-wired, no code reference.
LeanDropCount.cs:7 documents that it counts drops of GameObjects carrying LeanSelectableDrop. Inspector-wired, no code reference.
LeanPinchCamera.cs:68 documents MultiplyZoom as a target for LeanMouseWheel scrolling. Inspector-wired, no code reference.

layers.name: Gesture Detection & Recognition
layers.description: Single-finger gesture detectors and stroke recognisers - the components a developer drops in to turn raw finger lifecycle (down, up, held, tap, flick, swipe, edge swipe) into UnityEvents, plus the shape-matching, gesture-arbitration and stroke-replay pieces built on top of the same stroke data.

layers.name: Multi-Finger Gestures
layers.description: The LeanMulti* family: components that filter a set of simultaneous fingers and emit a measured value - pinch ratio, twist angle, directional distance, pull offset, per-frame delta - or fire on multi-finger down/up/held/tap/swipe. Grouped because they all share the same finger-filter configuration and float/Vector event contract designers wire in the Inspector.

layers.name: Selection & Picking
layers.description: Everything that answers "which object did the player choose": the drag-select and selection-box multi-selection tools, the lightweight LeanPick/LeanPickable raycast pair, and the LeanSelectable companion behaviours (dial, torque, pressure scale, centroid, hold/selected timers, the match-3 grid block reference). LeanSelectSelf.cs lives here too - it is a gutted 26-byte stub with no code and no edges, but its name and its surviving editor class belong to this selection cluster, so this is where a developer would look for it.

layers.name: Drag & Drop
layers.description: The only interface-based cluster in the package: IDropHandler defines the drop-target contract, LeanDrop and LeanDropCount implement it (raising dropped/match/unmatch events), and LeanSelectableDrop raycasts under a released selectable to find a handler. These four are genuinely coupled in code rather than only through the Inspector.

layers.name: Transform, Physics & Mesh Manipulation
layers.description: Drag-driven manipulation of scene content: translating Transforms and Rigidbodies (3D, 2D, along a surface or path), deforming and vertex-colouring meshes, rendering a drag as a line, and spawning a prefab under the finger. Grouped by effect - these are the components that actually change the world, as opposed to the ones that only report input.

layers.name: Canvas / UI Input Variants
layers.description: The five *Canvas subclasses, kept together rather than filed with their world-space base classes because they share one distinct concern: restricting finger detection to the RectTransform they are attached to via Unity UI raycasting. They are the only components in the package coupled to the UI system, and a developer choosing between world-space and canvas-space input makes that decision once, here.

layers.name: Camera & Viewport Control
layers.description: Gesture-to-camera components: pinch zoom (orthographic size or field of view, with damping and clamping), two-finger twist rotation, and mouse-wheel input as its desktop equivalent. Separate from the gesture detectors because these consume a gesture and drive the camera themselves instead of exposing an event.

layers.name: Package Definition & Documentation
layers.description: The asmdef that compiles these scripts into the LeanTouchPlus assembly, the UPM manifest declaring the LeanCommon/LeanTouch dependencies, and the bundled HTML manual cataloguing every demo scene - the non-code shell that makes the component library installable and discoverable.

tour.title: Start With The Manual
tour.description: There is no README here; the author's own manual is Documentation.html, and it is the single best map of this package. It is a catalog of every demo scene in Touch+/Examples, each introducing one component at a time, and it opens by telling you this asset is an extension to Lean Touch and that you should read the base Lean Touch documentation too. Do not open the raw HTML for reading (most of its 187 KB is base64-embedded fonts) - open it in a browser, or read the stripped text at .ua/intermediate/documentation-text.txt.

tour.title: What The Package Actually Is
tour.description: package.json declares com.cwilkes.lean.touch-plus and LeanTouchPlus.asmdef declares what it compiles into and against. The important takeaway is what is NOT here: LeanTouch, LeanGesture, LeanSelectable, LeanFingerData, LeanSwipeBase, LeanFingerFilter and CwEditor all live in the sibling LeanTouch, LeanCommon, LeanCommonPlus and CW.Common packages. Almost every file in this package extends a base class you will have to go read elsewhere.
tour.languageLesson: A Unity .asmdef turns a folder into its own compiled assembly. Its 'references' list is a hard compile boundary: code in this assembly can only see the assemblies named there, which is why that dependency list is the fastest way to find where the base classes live.

tour.title: Anatomy Of One Component
tour.description: LeanFingerHeld is the specimen to learn the house style from, and at 282 lines it is one of the few in-package base classes. Read it once carefully and you can read the other 54 files at a glance: a MonoBehaviour with serialized tuning fields (MinimumAge, MaximumMovement), public UnityEvent hooks it invokes, a private nested FingerData : LeanFingerData class holding per-finger state, and then - in the same file - a #if UNITY_EDITOR block containing a sibling LeanFingerHeld_Editor : CwEditor class under namespace Lean.Touch.Editor. 54 of the 55 scripts follow exactly that shape.
tour.languageLesson: C# lets a single .cs file declare several types in several namespaces, and #if UNITY_EDITOR strips the editor half from player builds. That is why runtime code and its custom Inspector live side by side here instead of in a separate Editor/ folder - one file per feature, zero shipped editor code.

tour.title: The Canvas Suffix Convention
tour.description: A *Canvas suffix means: same behaviour as the base component, but raycast against RectTransform UI elements instead of world colliders. LeanFingerHeldCanvas is 42 lines and fits on one screen - it exists only to re-scope its parent. Once you have seen one, the other four need no reading; recognising the suffix saves you opening five files.

tour.title: Where The Wiring Lives
tour.description: This is the most important thing to understand before you go looking for anything: the whole package has roughly ten code-level cross-file relationships. Components are composed by dragging UnityEvent connections in the Unity Inspector, which leaves no trace in source. The manual's own example is here - LeanMouseWheel's OnDelta event is connected to LeanPinchCamera's MultiplyZoom method to add scroll-wheel zoom. Nothing in either file mentions the other. If you expect to find the wiring in code you will waste hours; open the demo scenes instead.
tour.languageLesson: UnityEvent is serialized late-bound invocation: the target object and method name are stored in the scene or prefab asset, not in code. Compile-time tooling - grep, call graphs, rename refactors - cannot see through it, so scene files are part of the source you must read.

tour.title: Single-Finger Gesture Detection
tour.description: With the conventions from Steps 3-5 in hand, the rest of the package is a catalog you can browse. This family covers the single-finger lifecycle: LeanFirstDown and LeanLastUp fire only for the first finger down and the last finger up, while the two tap variants separate a quick tap from an expired one so single and double taps stop interfering with each other. LeanFingerFlick detects a fast release. They are siblings, not layers - none of them imports another.

tour.title: The Multi-Finger Family
tour.description: LeanMultiUpdate is the workhorse of this group at 354 lines: a general-purpose per-frame multi-finger driver that other components hang off. Around it sit the specific recognisers - pinch, twist, swipe, tap - each exposing its measurement as a UnityEvent payload (LeanMultiTwist.OnTwistDegrees is the one the manual wires into rotation components). LeanMultiPull, LeanMultiDirection, LeanMultiDown, LeanMultiUp and LeanMultiHeld round out the set on the same pattern.

tour.title: Shape Recognition
tour.description: The most algorithmically interesting corner of the package, and one of the few genuine in-code dependencies: LeanShape defines a point list describing a drawable shape, and LeanShapeDetector matches finger paths against it through ConvertPoints, FitShape and CalculateMatch. Its DistanceThreshold and ErrorThreshold settings tune how forgiving the match is. LeanReplayFinger records and replays a finger path, which is what makes this pair testable without a touchscreen.

tour.title: Selection And Picking
tour.description: Two distinct routes to answering 'which object did the finger hit'. LeanPick plus LeanPickable is the lightweight one, bypassing the selection system entirely - and it is the package's one verified call edge: LeanPick.SelectScreenPosition invokes LeanPickable.InvokePick. The heavier route builds on the external LeanSelectable base: LeanDragSelect selects by dragging across objects, and LeanSelectionBox spawns a UI rectangle prefab and selects everything inside it.

tour.title: Drag And Drop: The One Interface
tour.description: This is the only interface-based cluster in the package, and the only place where classic OO polymorphism shows up. IDropHandler is nine lines; LeanDrop and LeanDropCount implement it as receivers, while LeanSelectableDrop is the draggable side that gets dropped onto them. It is worth reading precisely because it contrasts with everything else: here the contract is in code and greppable, whereas everywhere else it is a UnityEvent buried in a scene file.
tour.languageLesson: An interface with two implementors is the honest use of the feature: the drop receiver is looked up at runtime by type, so the caller cannot know the concrete class. Compare it with a UnityEvent achieving the same decoupling with no type safety at all - each trades checking for flexibility in the opposite direction.

tour.title: Making Things Move
tour.description: The output end of every gesture: components that actually change an object once something drives them. Translation along a path, Rigidbody and Rigidbody2D movement for physics-driven objects, torque from a drag, and mesh-level effects that deform vertices or paint vertex colours. Each is a UnityEvent target, so any recogniser from Steps 6-8 can drive any of them - which is the composability the manual advertises.

tour.title: Now Read A Real One
tour.description: Three larger, self-contained components to test whether the conventions have stuck. LeanSpawnWithFinger instantiates a prefab under a finger and keeps updating its transform while the finger moves; LeanDragLine draws a line from a finger; LeanSelectableBlock snaps a selected object to a grid. Each has real internal logic (LeanSpawnWithFinger routes both Spawn and Update through UpdateSpawnedTransform) rather than being a thin event wrapper, and none of the three depends on the other two.

tour.title: Do Not Trust The Filenames
tour.description: A short honest closer. Three files declare an editor class copy-pasted from an unrelated component: LeanMultiTwist.cs contains LeanDestroy_Editor, LeanPickable.cs contains LeanSelectSelf_Editor, and LeanSelectableTime.cs contains LeanPlane_Editor. LeanSelectSelf.cs is a 26-byte gutted stub - a byte-order mark and the comment // Remove. None of this breaks at runtime, but it means filename-to-class-name symmetry is not guaranteed here: when you search this package, search for the type you want, not the file you expect it in.
